title: Extension by zero of module objects
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and $j\colon U\to X$ an open immersion.
The *extension by zero of module objects* is

$$
j_!:=j^{\mathrm{lin}}_!\circ\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_j}\colon
\Mod_{\Lambda_U}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_X},
$$

restriction of scalars along $\alpha_j\colon j^*\Lambda_X\to\Lambda_U$
([sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]) followed by the
linear extension by zero of [def-sfb-module-linear-open-lower-shriek]. The underlying
sheaf of $j_!M$ is the extension by zero $j^{\Ab}_!M$ of the underlying sheaf of $M$,
and $j_!$ is additive and exact.

proof.text: Put $A=j^*\Lambda_X$, $B=\Lambda_U$. The abelian-sheaf categories on $U,X$ are abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]; their tensor factors are additive and preserve colimits by [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-closed]. Thus [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] gives abelian categories of $A$-modules and $B$-modules on $U$ and $\Lambda_X$-modules on $X$.

source.place: Ambient hypotheses of the first sentence and the concluding additivity clause

proof.text: The coefficient map $\alpha_j:A\to B$ is a ring morphism by [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]. Apply [lem-sfb-modobj-restriction-finite-exact] in the abelian-sheaf category on $U$: it has finite limits and colimits, and both $A\otimes-$ and $B\otimes-$ preserve finite colimits by step 1. Hence $R=\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_j}$ preserves finite limits and colimits.

source.place: First sentence: finite exactness of restriction, now a separate statement-only lemma

proof.text: Let $L=j^{\mathrm{lin}}_!$ be [def-sfb-module-linear-open-lower-shriek] and define $j_!=L\circ R$. Restriction fixes underlying objects and maps by [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], while the underlying functor of $L$ is $j^{\Ab}_!$. Therefore $j_!M$ has underlying sheaf $j^{\Ab}_!M$; equality on underlying maps makes the identification natural.

source.place: Displayed composite and underlying-sheaf clause; first two proof sentences

proof.text: The functor $L$ is exact by [def-sfb-module-linear-open-lower-shriek], so it preserves finite limits and colimits by [def-galois-exact-functor]. Since the three module categories are abelian, [lem-sfb-preserving-colimits-additive] applies to both $R$ and $L$. Hence $j_!(h+k)=L(Rh+Rk)=j_!h+j_!k$, proving additivity. A finite limit cone remains limiting first under $R$ and then under $L$; the same holds for finite colimit cocones. Thus $L\circ R=j_!$ is exact by the cited definition.

source.place: Last sentence: short assembly of additive and exact functors

proof_origin.place: Restriction-then-linear-extension route; finite exactness of restriction isolated in lem-sfb-modobj-restriction-finite-exact, additivity supplied by the existing finite-colimit lemma.

noncomputable def openImmersionLowerShriek :
    Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology U) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ U) ⥤
      Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ X) :=
lean.note: Exact existing upstream definition, read from the current server source with scompile.py --source. For Λ : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) Ab.{u + 1} with [MonObj Λ] [IsCommMonObj Λ], schemes U X : Scheme.{u}, j : U ⟶ X and [IsOpenImmersion j], openImmersionLowerShriek is Mod.comap (condensedPullbackHom Λ j) followed by linearOpenImmersionLowerShriek Λ j, exactly restriction of scalars along α_j followed by linear extension by zero. The listed companion declarations give the underlying-sheaf equality and additivity/exactness (finite limits, finite colimits, and homology preservation). This matches every clause of the node statement; no duplicate module is needed.
